sentiment.rationale: The document reports a strong operational turnaround with revenue up 57% to $23.9B, GAAP EPS of $10.23 (including a $9.6B gain), and positive free cash flow of $0.4B. Management expresses confidence in the recovery, citing record backlogs, production rate increases, and a clear path to $10B free cash flow. However, the score is tempered by ongoing losses in BCA and BDS segments, a new KC-46A charge, and the recognition that the company has 'not fully turned the corner.'

summary.revenue: Fourth quarter revenue of $23.9 billion, up 57% year-over-year, reflecting improved operational performance and higher commercial delivery volume. Full year revenue of $89.5 billion, up 34%.
summary.eps: GAAP diluted EPS of $10.23 for Q4 2025, compared to ($5.46) in Q4 2024. Core EPS (non-GAAP) of $9.92, compared to ($5.90). The Q4 EPS primarily reflects a $9.6 billion gain on sale associated with closing the Digital Aviation Solutions transaction, which increased EPS by $11.83.
summary.guidance: 2026 free cash flow guidance of $1 billion to $3 billion. Management stated they 'continue to believe the $10 billion free cash flow mark is very attainable.' BCA deliveries expected to be up approximately 10% in 2026, with 737 deliveries around 500 aircraft and 787 deliveries between 90-100 aircraft.
summary.margin: Q4 2025 GAAP operating margin of 36.7% (includes $9.6B gain), compared to (24.7%) in Q4 2024. Core operating margin (non-GAAP) of 35.6%, compared to (26.5%). BCA operating margin of (5.6%), BDS operating margin of (6.8%), BGS operating margin of 202.4% (includes gain).
key_risks: KC-46A program: $565 million loss in Q4 driven by higher estimated production support and supply chain costs.
777X engine durability issue identified during inspection; working with GE to understand root cause and corrective action.
Delayed certification and first delivery on 777X program impacting cash flow; net cash use expected to turn positive only in 2029.
Customer considerations and excess advances on 737 and 787 programs due to prior delivery delays.
DOJ payment expected in 2026, sliding from 2025.
Potential tariff risks and geopolitical volatility, particularly regarding deliveries into China and Europe.
Spirit AeroSystems integration risk and its $1 billion unfavorable cash flow impact in 2026.
key_opportunities: Record total company backlog of $682 billion, including over 6,100 commercial airplanes.
737 production rate increased to 42 per month, on track to 47 later in 2026, with new North Line in Everett for rates above 47.
787 program stabilizing at rate 8, targeting rate 10 later in 2026, with factory expansion in Charleston.
777X booked 202 orders in 2025, second highest annual total since program launch; first delivery still anticipated in 2027.
BDS secured record backlog of $85 billion, including transformational win for U.S. Air Force sixth-generation fighter (F-47).
BGS record annual orders of $28 billion and record backlog of $30 billion.
Management believes $10 billion free cash flow is 'very attainable' as temporary headwinds resolve.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: CEO Kelly Ortberg stated: 'We made significant progress on our recovery in 2025 and have set the foundation to keep our momentum going in the year ahead,' and CFO Jay Malave said the $10 billion free cash flow mark is 'very attainable,' reflecting a confident tone despite acknowledged challenges.

review_flags.reason: The score of 0.55 reflects strong operational improvement and positive guidance, but the company still reports segment losses and a new KC-46A charge. A reviewer may wish to assess whether the positive tone is fully justified given the ongoing risks.
